title: Digital Lending Efficacy on Debt Management of Wage Earners
authors: Esperanza, D. N.; Bithay, L. L.; Jesus, J. B.; Ople-Alviola, C.; Sumilhig, J. M.; Basilisco, G. L.
tldr: Perceived quality of digital lending significantly affects PAY and CAUTION debt behaviors, while frequent usage negatively relates to STOP practices, revealing a behavioral paradox in Cebu City wage earners.
problem_and_motivation: Digital lending is growing rapidly in emerging economies, but its effectiveness in shaping responsible debt management behaviors among wage earners is not well understood.
approach: Descriptive-correlational design with 100 wage earners in Cebu City using simple random sampling.
Guided by Technology Acceptance Model and Financial Capability Framework.
Measures digital lending: accessibility, usage, and quality.
Three debt strategies: STOP (budget restraint), PAY (repayment), CAUTION (informed borrowing).
findings: Perceived quality of digital lending significantly affects PAY and CAUTION behaviors.
Frequent usage negatively related to STOP practices, revealing a behavioral paradox.
Accessibility did not have significant effects on debt management.
Digital lending alone is insufficient to ensure responsible borrowing.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Identifies a behavioral paradox where greater digital lending access may reduce financial restraint. Shows perceived quality matters more than accessibility for responsible borrowing. The STOP-PAY-CAUTION framework offers structured debt management evaluation.
directly_justifies: Perceived quality of digital lending promotes responsible borrowing.
Frequent digital lending usage reduces budget restraint.
Digital lending requires financial education for responsible use.
limits: Sample of 100 wage earners in one city limits generalizability.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 domains. Flagged 1.C, 2.A, 13.B (high), 7.B (medium). Rejected algorithmic topics as this is a survey-based behavioral study.

limitations: Sample limited to 100 wage earners in Cebu City.
Urban focus limits applicability to rural areas.
remember_this: Perceived quality of digital lending promotes responsible borrowing.
Frequent usage reduces budget restraint (behavioral paradox).
Digital lending requires financial education for responsible use.
